title: One zero line makes the forecast miss readable
body:
scale numeric r.date nice=false
scale numeric r.error zero=true
unit Hours at=92,148 size=820x350 axisTitles.x="UTC supplied hour" axisTitles.y="Actual minus forecast (MWh)" {
  label show=false
  path Error x=r.date y=r.error orderField=r.date strokeWidth=1.3
}
rule "On forecast" at=6,0 unit=Hours axis=y value.value=0
encoding: A chronological path encodes the signed MWh difference. A constant horizontal rule marks equality.
order: Ascending supplied UTC timestamp; no smoothing.
baseline: Zero is actual equals forecast.
scale: Shared linear MWh scale includes zero. The x scale uses real timestamps.
information_loss: The original served-demand and forecast levels disappear. The source notebook preserves both.

title: Clock-hour error cells need their coverage context
body:
scale position clock.hour_label
scale value Miss transform=linear
unit Months at=40,165 size=740x42 {
  repeat clock.month_label arrangement=rows gap=75 order=label
  label width=155 fontSize=13
  strip Error position=clock.hour_label valueScale=Miss aggregation=average measureField=clock.abs_error encoding=color
}
legend "Mean absolute error (MWh)" at=200,115 unit=Months mark=Error scale=Miss
encoding: Each cell encodes the mean absolute miss for one supplied month and UTC clock hour.
order: Months and padded clock labels follow calendar order.
baseline: Absolute error starts at zero; an empty cell is not zero.
scale: One shared linear color ramp; native value ramps may rescale under filtering.
information_loss: Cell means hide individual hours. The accompanying clock notebook exposes hours per cell.

title: A historical CO2 rise, one available-week mean per year
body:
scale numeric annual.year nice=false
scale numeric annual.mean zero=false
unit Years at=88,150 size=820x345 axisTitles.x="Supplied year" axisTitles.y="Annual mean CO2 (ppmv)" {
  label show=false
  path Mean x=annual.year y=annual.mean orderField=annual.year
  point Annual x=annual.year y=annual.mean radius=2
}
encoding: A thin path and dots show the available-week annual means. Dots retain the annual sampling unit.
order: Chronological years; no endpoint extension.
baseline: The concentration axis is not forced to zero because position, not bar length, encodes value.
scale: One linear concentration scale; partial endpoint years remain included and documented.
information_loss: Seasonality and week-level coverage disappear in the annual mean; they remain in the linked source material.

title: The middle half of centered CO2 weeks, month by month
encoding: Native unweighted quartiles form a band and medians are connected across ordered months.
order: Padded month labels preserve January-to-December order.
baseline: Zero is each underlying year’s measured-week mean, not a universal absolute concentration.
scale: Shared linear residual scale; the summary is recomputed from eligible live rows.
information_loss: This representation hides the absolute concentration trend and each individual week. Means quoted in the companion are distinct from the drawn medians.

title: Two warm-water windows on one unshifted clock
body:
scale numeric episodes.episode_month nice=false min=1 max=24
scale numeric episodes.anomaly zero=true
unit Windows at=90,155 size=820x330 axisTitles.x="Month since January of first year" axisTitles.y="Niño 1+2 anomaly (degrees C)" {
  label show=false
  path Anomalies x=episodes.episode_month y=episodes.anomaly orderField=episodes.episode_month seriesField=episodes.episode colorField=episodes.episode
  point Months x=episodes.episode_month y=episodes.anomaly radius=2 colorField=episodes.episode
}
rule "1981–2010 monthly reference" at=5,0 unit=Windows axis=y value.value=0
legend Windows at=110,535 unit=Windows mark=Anomalies
encoding: Two colored paths retain the monthly anomalies in the predeclared two-year windows.
order: Each path runs from January of its first year; peaks are not shifted into alignment.
baseline: Zero is the selected calendar-month climatology.
scale: Shared linear Celsius anomaly scale and identical 1–24 month index.
information_loss: A two-window comparison cannot establish the distribution of all events or a causal explanation.

title: A temperature range is not a confidence interval
encoding: A supplied min–max band surrounds an annual mean path. The band uses measured monthly extremes.
order: Calendar-year order, with no smooth curves or forecast extension.
baseline: No artificial zero baseline for a position-encoded Celsius series.
scale: One shared linear temperature scale spans the mean and both supplied bounds.
information_loss: The month that produced an extreme is lost. The band is not sampling uncertainty, a prediction interval, or a native forecast.

title: Annual sunspot activity has different distributions across eras
encoding: One native kernel-density trace summarizes annual sunspot numbers in each broad historical span.
order: Half-century labels in ascending order; the final span is incomplete.
baseline: The horizontal scale includes zero; ridge height is a shared density peak, not an observation count.
scale: A shared activity domain allows horizontal comparison. Density peaks may rescale with active filters in this baseline.
information_loss: Smoothing hides individual years and depends on bandwidth. Unequal era counts remain in the source notebook.

title: A comparison boundary does not make a causal experiment
body:
scale numeric r.year nice=false
scale numeric r.volume zero=false
unit Years at=90,155 size=820x335 axisTitles.x=Year axisTitles.y="Annual flow at Aswan (10^8 m3)" {
  label show=false
  path Flow x=r.year y=r.volume orderField=r.year
  point Annual x=r.year y=r.volume radius=2
}
rule "1898 comparison boundary" at=6,-335 unit=Years value.value=1898
encoding: An annual-volume path keeps wet and dry years visible, with a fixed vertical comparison boundary.
order: Chronological source years.
baseline: The boundary defines a descriptive split; the volume axis is a position scale, not a bar-length baseline.
scale: One shared linear annual-volume scale.
information_loss: A single path cannot adjust for climate, gauge changes, or other confounders. The line is not an estimated intervention effect.

title: GDP growth folded around zero, not the GDP level
encoding: A native horizon mark folds positive and negative annualized quarterly growth into compact bands.
order: Quarter order, with the initial unavailable change left null.
baseline: Zero means no quarterly GDP change; the horizon is not rebased to its first observation.
scale: Shared growth magnitude; three bands are a display choice, not economic categories.
information_loss: Folding reduces direct vertical reading and can obscure the size of extremes. The original growth line is the necessary companion.

title: Decade clouds complicate a pooled economic relationship
body:
scale numeric r.unemp zero=false
scale numeric r.infl zero=true
unit Quarters at=90,155 size=790x325 axisTitles.x="Unemployment rate (%)" axisTitles.y="Source annualized inflation (%)" {
  label show=false
  point Observations x=r.unemp y=r.infl colorField=r.decade radius=3
}
legend Decades at=110,535 unit=Quarters mark=Observations
encoding: Individual quarterly observations are positioned by unemployment and inflation and colored by decade.
order: No connecting path: file order is not a trajectory through this two-variable space.
baseline: Inflation includes a zero reference in the domain; source initial placeholder remains identifiable in the table.
scale: Shared linear percentage scales for every decade.
information_loss: The graphic discards temporal adjacency. Pooled or grouped proximity is not a causal policy relationship.

title: Firm investment paths on one absolute scale
body:
scale numeric r.year nice=false ticks=ends
scale numeric r.invest zero=true
unit Firms at=34,145 size=715x42 axisTitles.x=Year {
  repeat r.firm arrangement=rows gap=27 order=label
  label width=195 fontSize=12
  path Investment x=r.year y=r.invest orderField=r.year
}
encoding: A repeated path for each firm shows recorded investment using the same vertical scale.
order: Firm names alphabetically; years ascend inside each row.
baseline: A shared zero baseline makes absolute investment heights comparable.
scale: Shared linear source 1947-dollar units; no unverified multiplier added.
information_loss: Smaller firms become compressed. That is an honest consequence of absolute comparison, not a reason to secretly rescale each row.

title: An indexed sparkline grid trades magnitude for shape
body:
scale numeric r.year nice=false ticks=ends
scale numeric r.invest_index domain=instance zero=false
unit Firms at=65,160 size=250x120 axisTitles.x=Year {
  repeat r.firm arrangement=grid columns=3 gap=68 order=label
  label fontSize=12
  path Indexed x=r.year y=r.invest_index orderField=r.year
  point Latest x=r.year y=r.invest_index orderField=r.year show=last radius=3
}
encoding: A grid of indexed investment paths gives each firm room to show its own trajectory, with the latest observation marked.
order: Alphabetic firm order, chronological years within each path.
baseline: Each index begins at 100 by construction; per-panel vertical domains are explicitly allowed to differ.
scale: Common time scale, intentionally separate value scales. Heights must not be compared between panels.
information_loss: Absolute investment and directly comparable growth amplitude are lost. This is an explicit shape-reading alternative, not an improvement for every task.

title: An influential plant observation is not automatically an error
encoding: The left panel shows original observed pairs; the right panel shows one refitted slope per omitted observation.
order: Original row sequence identifies omitted points; it is not a verified date sequence.
baseline: Loss includes zero; the slope panel uses a position scale centered on the observed range, not zero.
scale: Separate labeled scales reflect different quantities. The panels are not dual axes on one plot.
information_loss: The paired display does not show multivariable controls or prediction uncertainty. No row is removed from the reference data.

title: Each household remains a dot in the food-share comparison
encoding: One dot per household is spread into a swarm along its food-share value within its income quartile.
order: Quartiles ascend from lower to higher income. Vertical dot displacement prevents overlap and has no measured meaning.
baseline: Zero is no food expenditure as a share of income.
scale: One shared linear percentage scale across the quartiles.
information_loss: The original income and franc expenditure disappear, and swarm displacement is not an extra variable.

title: Long strikes without crushing the short ones
encoding: Each strike is one swarmed dot on a logarithmic duration scale, separated by the declared production-context split.
order: Context labels alphabetically; within-row vertical displacement has no data meaning.
baseline: A log scale has no zero. Every supplied duration is positive and retained.
scale: Shared log day scale, so equal horizontal distances represent ratios rather than day differences.
information_loss: The spacing no longer communicates additive days. Group separation is descriptive, not an estimate of a production effect.

title: A source-rate spread, with the subtraction made explicit
body:
scale numeric r.date nice=false
scale numeric r.spread zero=true
unit Quarters at=92,165 size=810x325 axisTitles.x="Historical Danish quarter" axisTitles.y="Bond minus deposit (source rate fractions)" {
  label show=false
  path Spread x=r.date y=r.spread orderField=r.date
  point Observed x=r.date y=r.spread radius=2.5
}
rule Equality at=6,0 unit=Quarters axis=y value.value=0
encoding: A single path encodes bond rate minus deposit rate, with each supplied quarter marked.
order: Calendar-quarter order.
baseline: Zero means equal source rates.
scale: Linear source fractions, not silently formatted as percentages or currency.
information_loss: The two source levels are removed by subtraction. The companion notebook retains them and explains the historical scope.

title: Two fertility endpoints, the same country cohort
body:
scale numeric paired.year nice=false ticks=ends
scale numeric paired.fertility zero=true
unit Countries at=68,175 size=240x130 axisTitles.y="Births per woman" {
  repeat paired.country arrangement=grid columns=3 gap=75 order=label
  label fontSize=12
  path Change x=paired.year y=paired.fertility orderField=paired.year
  point Endpoints x=paired.year y=paired.fertility radius=3
}
encoding: A small paired slope chart for each country preserves its two endpoint observations.
order: Country labels alphabetically; 1960 precedes 2011 on every panel.
baseline: Shared zero on the fertility-rate scale; no country-specific rescaling.
scale: Common linear births-per-woman and endpoint-year scales.
information_loss: The connecting segment is an endpoint comparison, not interpolation of the intervening annual path.

title: The pace of fertility change is not uniform across decades
body:
scale position decades.decade
scale value Pace center=#f7f7f7 colors=#2166ac,#b2182b transform=linear
unit Countries at=34,185 size=675x30 {
  repeat decades.country arrangement=rows gap=15 order=label
  label width=240 fontSize=12
  strip Pace position=decades.decade valueScale=Pace aggregation=average measureField=decades.annual_change encoding=color
}
legend "Births per woman per elapsed year" at=300,118 unit=Countries mark=Pace scale=Pace
encoding: Color encodes the first-to-last annualized change for each country-decade.
order: Country labels alphabetically; decade categories chronologically.
baseline: Zero is no first-to-last change. Each decade difference divides by nine elapsed years.
scale: Shared signed linear ramp; live strip scales may rescale under active filters.
information_loss: Within-decade reversals and endpoint levels are lost. Color is less precise than position for comparing close values.

title: Petal lengths, one measured flower at a time
encoding: A common-scale swarm preserves each measured petal length within its supplied species group.
order: Alphabetic species order; vertical displacement is overlap avoidance, not another measurement.
baseline: Zero is included because centimetres have a meaningful origin.
scale: Shared linear length scale across all species.
information_loss: Petal width and the sepal measurements disappear, so separation here is not a validated classification result.

title: Thirteen assays cannot share one raw value ruler
encoding: Each assay panel shows native unweighted quartiles and medians across the three cultivar groups.
order: Assay field names alphabetically; cultivar labels in their supplied order.
baseline: No universal zero or raw-unit baseline is imposed across unlike assays.
scale: Each assay intentionally has its own linear value domain. Axis heights must not be compared across assays.
information_loss: The individual wine identity and cross-assay covariance disappear in grouped summaries. Source assay units are not fully specified by the publisher.

title: A common starting index is an analytical choice
body:
scale numeric indexed.year nice=false
scale numeric indexed.value zero=false
unit Years at=90,165 size=800x315 axisTitles.x=Year axisTitles.y="First supplied year = 100" {
  label show=false
  path Indices x=indexed.year y=indexed.value orderField=indexed.year seriesField=indexed.series colorField=indexed.series
}
rule "Initial index" at=6,0 unit=Years axis=y value.value=100
legend Series at=110,535 unit=Years mark=Indices
encoding: Three colored paths compare proportional movement after each series is rebased to its first value.
order: Chronological source years, without smoothing.
baseline: The reference 100 is imposed by rebasing; it is not an independently observed economic equality.
scale: One shared linear index scale for all three series.
information_loss: Original counts and nominal-output units are erased. Nominal GNP growth still includes price-level change.

title: Separate historical counts instead of inventing a rate
encoding: Two independently labeled historical count paths keep distinct populations separate.
order: Calendar years in both panels.
baseline: Both value scales include zero; these are counts, not a computed labor-force share.
scale: Shared time domain with separate count domains, explicitly not a stacked total or dual-axis overlay.
information_loss: Comparing panel heights without reading the scales is invalid. No denominator for an official unemployment rate is supplied.

title: Scoring and conceding form different group-stage profiles
body:
scale numeric teams.goals_for zero=true
scale numeric teams.goals_against zero=true
unit Teams at=95,165 size=785x320 axisTitles.x="Group-stage goals scored" axisTitles.y="Group-stage goals conceded" {
  label show=false
  point Profiles x=teams.goals_for y=teams.goals_against colorField=teams.group radius=5
}
legend Groups at=110,535 unit=Teams mark=Profiles
encoding: One team is one point positioned by goals for and against, with group membership encoded by color.
order: No line connects teams; listing order has no measured meaning.
baseline: Both goal counts use zero baselines.
scale: Shared linear goal-count scales. Equal scores can overlap and remain separate source records.
information_loss: Opponent strength, match sequence, and advancement tie-break rules are not encoded. Points are not independent because teams share matches.

title: One cell is one match, not one goal
encoding: A waffle cell represents one group match and its color distinguishes a draw from a decisive score.
order: Groups alphabetically; category order remains consistent across repeats.
baseline: Counts start with no cells; the graphic is not normalized to a synthetic hundred-cell population.
scale: Equal-size cells preserve equal match weights across groups.
information_loss: Goal totals and the closeness of decisive matches are lost. The cells encode match counts rather than goals or team appearances.

title: Two catalogue dates do not necessarily make a lifespan
body:
scale numeric r.date_span zero=true
unit Entities at=40,200 size=705x90 axisTitles.x="Recorded date span (years; not necessarily lifespan)" {
  repeat r.entity arrangement=rows gap=80 order=label
  label width=210 fontSize=12
  point Records x=r.date_span spread=swarm radius=4
}
note "Blank death dates remain missing. This is an alphabetic prefix of an old archive, not current biographies." at=75,540 leader=false
encoding: A swarmed dot row compares recorded date spans while separating the explicitly named family entity.
order: Entity labels alphabetically; source records are not ranked as human lifespans.
baseline: Zero is no difference between the supplied dates, not an inferred age at death.
scale: Shared linear year-span scale. Missing spans do not become zero-valued dots.
information_loss: The prefix is not representative. A blank death field supplies no current living-status information, and catalogue entities are not necessarily individuals.
